title: Small-data wave operators for Moyal nonlinear Schrodinger evolution in dimension two d with alpha greater than two d and real polynomial interaction without constant term, and without linear term when d is one or two
author: Bergfinnur Durhuus; Victor Gayral
work: The Scattering Problem for a Noncommutative Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
source_version: Official SIGMA 6 (2010) article 046, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2010.046; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: Classical dispersive norms are poorly behaved under the Moyal product, so standard small-data NLS scattering cannot be applied without constructing another analytic framework. The author obtains uniform oscillator-matrix propagation bounds by rewriting the heat kernel as Jacobi polynomials and applying a precisely stated uniform weighted bound. New weighted matrix-product and polynomial Lipschitz estimates then verify every hypothesis of the abstract nonlinear scattering theorem, yielding a concrete scattering space and the stated degree restrictions.

proof_review.note: Read complete Weyl/Moyal operator equation and self-adjoint weighted Laplacian setup2-4, exact scattering norm and integral equations4-5, full weighted matrix bounds Lemmas1-4 on7-8, heat-kernel/Jacobi identity Lemma5 and uniform dispersion Lemma6 on8-10, final weighted free estimate Theorem2 on12-13 and all four nonlinear scattering estimates and polynomial difference expansion13-15. Select Theorem3 for d>=1, alpha>2d and real polynomial F with no constant term and no linear term if d<=2. Small final/initial scattering data in Sigma_alpha give unique global continuous solutions and Hilbert-weighted asymptotic convergence; the stronger scattering-norm convergence is selected only under the additional absence of a linear term. Reed1976 Abstract non-linear wave equations Theorem16 is explicitly identified and its four hypotheses are fully written and verified here; the classical Jacobi uniform bound is precisely stated from Erdelyi-Magnus-Nevai1994. These are established foundations, not omitted new local cores. The diagonal arbitrary-data Theorem4, soliton existence and asymptotic completeness are uncounted. Exact selected statement and terminal proof pages rendered and visually inspected; physical headers/native ZIP members and source/license hashes checked. No independent mathematical reproof.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem3 in the source oscillator weighted Hilbert space H_alpha=L_{2,alpha}, b_mn=1+EuclideanNorm(m-n), and Sigma_alpha with norm ||phi||_{2,alpha}+sup_t abs(t)^(d/2)||exp(-it Delta_alpha)phi||_a. Let d>=1, alpha>2d, and F a real polynomial with F(0)=0, with zero linear coefficient when d=1 or2. There is delta>0 such that scattering data phi_plus/minus in Sigma_alpha of norm<delta have unique global continuous solutions of original equations(9)/(10), converging in H_alpha to free evolution as t goes to the corresponding infinity. If F also has zero linear coefficient, the free-frame difference converges in the full scattering norm. Theta>0 is absorbed into F as stated in the original equation; no large-data general or asymptotic completeness assertion.
